chunks: Do they say: 'He is a poet for whom we expect an adverse turn of fortune?'

key_terms.رَيْبَ الْمَنُونِ: Adverse turn of fortune / death / misfortune

ai.seo_question: What did the Quraysh mean by 'rib al-manun' in relation to Prophet Muhammad being a poet?
ai.summary: In this verse from Surah Al-Muddaththir, the Quraysh dismiss Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) as a poet, anticipating 'rib al-manun' (a sudden turn of fate or death) to invalidate his message. This reflects the pre-Islamic Arab belief that poets were possessed by jinn and thus vulnerable to their whims, a claim the Quran refutes by highlighting the Prophet's sanity and divine inspiration.
